title: mine evidence to extend FR_REGIONS for France
headline: The inherited claim that FR_REGIONS resolves state for 100% of France rows holds only for test_source1, which is 15.31% of French rows. At most 1,204,739 of 1,694,445 France test rows (71.10%) can resolve a state; 489,706 (28.90%) provably cannot, and a maximal French gazetteer recovers only 14,892 (0.88%). Root cause: test_s2/test_s3 encode French geography with DEPARTMENT names, not region names, and the departments they use are mostly absent from FR_REGIONS.
most_important_number_meaning: France test rows that provably cannot resolve any state via FR_REGIONS (28.90% of 1,694,445)

method.state_resolution_rule: normalize_address (normalize.py:314-353) matches state only on an exact whole-comma-component match: ck = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9& ]+',' ',c).replace('&',' and '); ck = ' '.join(ck.split()); if ck in smap
method.profile_alignment: build_profile.py:126-127 splits address on ADDR_SPLIT [,;] before counting addr_tokens, so profile token counts are the token multiset of the same components
method.bound: union bound: rows containing key <= min(token counts of key); summing over all 14 keys gives UB, an over-estimate. Per file resolvable <= min(UB, rows) and unresolved >= max(rows-UB, 0); the clamp is required because test_s1's UB (261,705) exceeds its row count (259,452)
method.caveat: component structure is discarded by the builder, so these are upper bounds on resolvable rows, not direct counts

secondary_finding_function_words.defect: ADDR_CANON_FR has no entries for de, la, du, des, le, les, d, l, e, s, a, c, p, f, h, m, g; France is 42x the US function-word rate
secondary_finding_function_words.impact: 16.3% of all French address token mass enters the IDF-weighted qa/sa features (features.py:120-123), diluting IDF weighting for every French pair
secondary_finding_function_words.recommendation: add de, la, du, des, le, les -> "" to ADDR_CANON_FR

accent_fragmentation_caveat.issue: build_profile.py:28 TOKEN_RE=[a-z0-9]+ runs on raw lower() WITHOUT accent stripping, but normalize_address DOES strip accents
accent_fragmentation_caveat.consequence: any recommended dictionary key must be written accent-stripped and lower-case to match the pipeline, not the profile

leetspeak_finding.conclusion: LEET (normalize.py:256) already covers every observed mixed-alpha-digit token; sequential numbers correctly stay digits

gaps: component boundaries discarded by build_profile.py:126-127; all numbers are upper bounds on resolvable rows, not direct counts
street-name vs toponym ambiguity unresolved for lorraine, alsace, normandie, grand est, gard, centre (marked LIKELY not CONFIRMED)
accent-blind tokenisation could mask low-frequency accented toponyms; cannot bound

France absent from all train_s* files, so cross-country false-positive risk of new FR_REGIONS keys on US rows is untested; 'nord' is the real collision risk (French dept AND English 'north' AND common US street name); US 'nord' count not measured
no precision measurement possible -- can bound rows that COULD resolve, never rows that WOULD falsely resolve
